segments.text: Mina has world-class proving. It also has one asset and almost no liquidity. Flare is the mirror image: a mature DeFi market, with no MINA in it.

So we made a Flare contract verify a Mina signature directly. No proof, no prover. Eight hundred thousand gas — three tenths of a cent. The same call on Ethereum is seventeen cents today, and thirty dollars on a busy afternoon. Ethereum isn't always expensive; it's unpredictable. A wallet you use daily can't be hostage to that.
Every transfer appends to one chain on Flare. The Flare Data Connector attests to its head once, and the escrow and all three token ports reuse that single proof.
No EVM key anywhere. The Flare address is derived from the Mina public key, so it exists before anything is deployed.
Everything here was built during the program. The verifier is two point two times faster than what we started from, measured at every step — including two optimisations we tried and rejected.
And it points somewhere. Mina is a proof system with a chain attached. The same rail that carries assets can carry proofs — verified on Flare for a fraction of running them there.
Deployed, public, running. Both directions, four assets, on Coston 2 and Mina devnet.
